cleared.check: L-842, task 1: every MegaETH PoolManager transaction that ends successfully with an ERC-20 still synced, and every later transaction of the same block that calls settle, settleFor or take.
cleared.result: None found. debug_traceTransaction with callTracer (https://mainnet.megaeth.com/rpc, mega-reth/v2.3.1-4499c42 at start and end) was run on 72,184 transactions: the 51,233 of the cycle 15 list (PoolManager logs or an ERC-20 Transfer to the PoolManager, blocks 7,009,653 to 32,770,383), 93 found by eth_getLogs for PoolManager logs and Transfers from or to the PoolManager from 32,770,384 to 32,814,962, and 20,858 more that appear only in Blockscout's internal transaction list (frames without a log, mostly failed). Every trace returned. The PoolManager frames were put in execution order with the reverted flag of the frame or an ancestor, and the source's transient model was replayed: sync(X) sets the synced currency and the reserves from the PoolManager's own balanceOf child call (src/libraries/CurrencyReserves.sol:27-32, src/PoolManager.sol:279-288), sync(0) and settle reset it (src/PoolManager.sol:283, 362), the state is empty at the start of each transaction. 36,875 completed ERC-20 syncs and 12,598 native ones; 54,803 completed settle calls each returned exactly what the model predicts (msg.value with nothing synced, balance rise since the sync otherwise, src/PoolManager.sol:349-364): zero mismatches. No successful transaction ends with an ERC-20 synced, so there is no later same-block settle to examine; 8,312 of 46,201 blocks hold several of these transactions. A settle credited from another transaction's sync would also show as a mismatch here, independently of finding the first transaction. Planted check (seed 18018, 200 sampled traces): dropping the first ERC-20 sync was detected 200 of 200 times, dropping the last settle left an ERC-20 synced or a mismatch 197 of 200 times (the other 3 end with a native settle). Not covered: a transaction that calls only sync and emits no log, makes no token transfer and is outside the Blockscout ranges read; it changes nothing unless a later settle is credited, and every later settle in the set was checked.

cleared.check: L-842, task 1 on Monad: PoolManager transactions that end with an ERC-20 synced, and settles of later transactions of the same block.
cleared.result: None found in a contiguous sample. Monad has about 650 PoolManager transactions per 1,000 blocks and eth_getLogs is limited to 100 blocks, so a full census was not possible from public endpoints. All 30,092 transactions with a PoolManager log or an ERC-20 Transfer from or to the PoolManager in blocks 125,250,001 to 125,295,000 (eth_getLogs in 450 windows of 100 blocks, https://rpc.monad.xyz and https://rpc-mainnet.monadinfra.com, Monad/0.16.7 at start and end) were traced with callTracer. 33,893 completed ERC-20 syncs, 24,580 syncs inside reverted frames, 42,244 completed settles, all equal to the model's value; no transaction ends with an ERC-20 synced; 6,771 of 16,675 blocks hold several. The client source explains why: every transaction, and every re-execution after a failed optimistic merge, runs on a fresh State built over the block state (execute_transaction.cpp lines 458 to 497), transient storage lives in AccountState::transient_storage_ (account_state.hpp line 70), and BlockState::merge copies only the account and storage_ of each address (block_state.cpp lines 194 to 250), so transient storage never reaches the next transaction.

cleared.check: MegaETH client source: where transient storage is cleared between transactions.
cleared.result: mega-evm (main, version 1.7.4; crates.io 1.7.2) pins revm 40.0.3, which uses revm-context 18.0.3. TLOAD and TSTORE are the stock host handlers wrapped for compute gas (mega-evm src/evm/instructions.rs lines 611-612 and 2205-2206) and the host delegates tstore and tload to the stock journal (src/evm/host.rs lines 90-91). That journal clears transient_storage in commit_tx, discard_tx and finalize (revm-context 18.0.3 src/journal/inner.rs lines 154, 188, 246). The sandbox that mega-evm uses for keyless deploys merges accounts and storage only, and its own path calls commit_tx (src/evm/execution.rs line 1023). EIP-1153 requires all transient values to be discarded at the end of the transaction. The producer itself is closed; the mined census above is the evidence that it behaves this way.

leadResults.answer: MegaETH: 72,184 PoolManager transactions traced (the 51,233 of cycle 15, all later ones to block 32,814,962, and those Blockscout lists without a log), Monad: 30,092 in blocks 125,250,001-125,295,000. None ends with an ERC-20 synced and every completed settle (54,803 and 42,244) returned what the source's transient model predicts, so no settle was credited from another transaction's sync. Controls: Unichain 28,261, BNB Chain 8,716, same result.

Pocket endpoints on all seven networks, the official Arbitrum One, Avalanche and Robinhood endpoints and nodereal on BNB Chain returned exactly the receipt count on every sampled block of every window they answered. The publicnode endpoints refused this client with HTTP 403, mainnet.optimism.io with 403 after one window and mainnet.base.org with 429, so those were not tested.

For PoolManager logs, bsc.api.pocket.network returned the same count as nodereal on all ten windows from block 45,970,610 to head (35,532 logs) and matched the receipts on every sampled block; on the cycle 17 window it returned 24,459 logs, as rpc-bsc.48.club did. The sNVB rebase history and the cycle 5 rows were not redone.

19,407 zero-value failed PoolManager calls in 8,959 transactions and 1,355 blocks enumerated over about 90% of the blocks before 31,861,608; three ranges remain and the blocks were traced but not re-run in the validator.
